paragraphs: In [Sotah 25a](https://www.sefaria.org/Sotah.25a.16-17): “Rabbi Yoshiyah said: Ze’ira told me three things in the name of the people of Jerusalem; and when I came to my colleagues in the South,” etc. In the [Jerusalem Talmud Sotah 4:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Sotah.4.2.2): “Rabbi Yoshiyah said: Ze’ira told me in the name of the people of Jerusalem.” In [Sifrei, Ki Tetze](https://www.sefaria.org/Sifrei_Devarim.218.7-8): “Ze’ira told me in the name of the people of Jerusalem; and when I came and presented it before Rabbi Yehudah ben Beteira,” etc. Hyman infers from this that he was early. And what we find in [Jerusalem Talmud Shekalim 3:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Shekalim.3.2.3), “Rabbi Ze’ira asked Rabbi Yoshiyah,” Hyman proposes “Rabbi Hoshaya.”[^1][^2]

notes.text: The linked Yerushalmi Sotah and Sifrei give “in the name of the people of Jerusalem.” The Bavli reads “from the people of Jerusalem,” which Davidson takes as describing Ze’ira. In the continuation, Rabbi Yoshiyah brings the rulings to his colleagues in the South in the Bavli and to Rabbi Yehudah ben Beteira in Sifrei.

The linked Shekalim has Ze’ira ask Rabbi Yoshiyah in a passage that Guggenheimer marks as an addition by a corrector. Hyman proposes Hoshaya there and infers an early date for the Ze’ira of the first chain.
